text: Android: allowBackup=true + EncryptedSharedPreferences = crash loop after backup restore

allowBackup=false is the clean choice here specifically because logout() already
treats the Room DB as disposable (it wipes it) and every bit of local state is
re-syncable from the server — so unlike most apps there's no user-data-loss
argument for keeping backup on. If you instead keep backup + exclusion rules,
exclude BOTH the "session" encrypted prefs AND the DataStore files (server_config
+ theme_preference), not just the Room DB: a restored DataStore syncCursor paired
with a session whose decryption just failed is its own mismatch.

Done in be9ef22. Went with note#1's endorsed simplest option: allowBackup=false
(all state re-syncable, logout() wipes the DB) rather than backup + exclusion
rules — plus the defensive SessionStore construction "regardless".

SessionStore.prefs now builds through a small extracted helper openWithRecovery(
build, onCorrupt): on GeneralSecurityException (AEADBadTagException etc. — keyset
undecryptable with this device's master key) or IOException, it deletes the
"session" prefs file and rebuilds once (fresh keysets under the current master
key); a second failure propagates. Net effect on a bad-keyset device: app starts
logged-out and re-syncs, no crash-loop.

Testability note: SessionStore itself has no unit tests here because Encrypted-
SharedPreferences needs a real Keystore that Robolectric can't provide (hence the
codebase's FakeSessionState). So I extracted the recovery control-flow into the
internal openWithRecovery and tested THAT directly (SessionStoreRecoveryTest, plain
JUnit) — success/no-cleanup, recover-on-GeneralSecurityException, recover-on-
IOException, second-failure-propagates. The manifest policy is guarded by
BackupPolicyTest (Robolectric confirms FLAG_ALLOW_BACKUP is cleared).

Residual (documented, acceptable): with allowBackup=false, cloud backup is off on
all API levels; device-to-device transfer on API 31+ can still copy app data, but
the defensive recovery means that path no longer crashes (worst case: re-login).
If someone later wants to also keep the token/DB off D2D entirely, add
dataExtractionRules with <device-transfer> exclusions — not needed for this bug.
Full-device e2e (actual restore) still falls under T-29's emulator pass.
Verified: :app:testDebugUnitTest + :app:lintDebug green.
